cases.name: weather: known user gets a real reading
cases.why: The whole point of the tool-calling pattern is that the agent fetches this.

cases.name: weather: reading comes from the tool, not the model
cases.why: The agent was once observed answering with a temperature it never fetched. The trace is how that stays visible.

cases.name: weather: unknown user gets nulls, not a plausible number
cases.why: A fabricated 0.0 reads as a real measurement and is worse than an error.

cases.name: rag: explains a pattern from the docs
cases.why: Retrieval has to surface the section that answers the question.

cases.name: rag: cites the section it drew from
cases.why: A passage with no provenance cannot be checked, which defeats the point of showing sources at all.

cases.name: rag: distinguishes neighbouring sections
cases.why: The corpus explains both what the trace measures and why its total differs from the sum, in adjacent sections using much the same vocabulary -- which is where similarity search goes wrong.

cases.name: rag: answers both halves of a two-part question
cases.why: A question spanning two sections must not be half-answered. How many searches that takes is the model's business: this case originally demanded two, and failed against an agent that got both answers with one well-phrased query -- which is better, not worse.

cases.name: rag: declines what the knowledge base cannot answer
cases.why: Answering from the model instead is the failure RAG exists to prevent.
